DESTINY-Gastric03, 'Ph1b/2 Study of the Safety and Efficacy of T-DXd Combinations in Advanced HER2-expressing Gastric Cancer': every arm is trastuzumab deruxtecan (other names 'DS-8201a, Enhertu') alone or with a partner, and capecitabine, 5-FU, oxaliplatin, cisplatin, durvalumab, pembrolizumab, volrustomig and rilvegostomig are the partners (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-10-28). The registry's first named intervention put the study on a 'Capecitabine' row, and the catalyst (id 301) carries asset_id 516, Imfinzi, while its indication row is Capecitabine's Stomach Neoplasms; neither is the drug under test. Enhertu is modelled (data/assumptions/azn_enhertu.csv); on this copy its asset (967) has no Stomach Neoplasms row, so the readout needs one. Enhertu is approved in previously treated HER2-positive gastric cancer, and this study tests first-line combinations

'A Study to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Co-Reconstituted TrenibotulinumtoxinE and OnabotulinumtoxinA in Adult Participants With Moderate to Severe Upper Facial Lines': onabotulinumtoxinA is Botox (BLA103000), one of the two toxins in the syringe and the active comparator arm. Upper facial lines are already on Botox Cosmetic's US label (DailyMed setid 485d9b71-6881-42c5-a620-a4360c7192ab: glabellar, lateral canthal and forehead lines), and abbv_botox.csv's base revenue includes Botox Cosmetic ($2,602mm of $6,371mm, FY2025 10-K 0001551152-26-000008), so the readout is a line extension inside revenue the book already holds: a layer is base_pool_overlap_pct 1.0. TrenibotulinumtoxinE alone (Boey) received a US complete response letter on manufacturing in April 2026 and EC approval in July 2026 (10-Q 0001551152-26-000026); no asset in the book carries it

STARGLO, 'Evaluating Glofitamab in Combination With Gemcitabine + Oxaliplatin vs Rituximab in Combination With Gemcitabine + Oxaliplatin': the agent under test is glofitamab and the rituximab arm is the comparator. The registry lists every ingredient of both arms as an intervention, so obinutuzumab, given as pre-treatment, placed the study on Gazyva and put another product's readout on Gazyva's book.

TETON-PPF, 'Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Inhaled Treprostinil in Subjects With Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis': an inhaled study sitting on Remodulin, which is parenteral and priced for pulmonary arterial hypertension. column4: MK-6482-016, 'Pembrolizumab Plus Lenvatinib in Combination With Belzutifan': the randomised variable is belzutifan, not pembrolizumab. Arm 1 is pembrolizumab + belzutifan + lenvatinib and Arm 2 is pembrolizumab + lenvatinib, so the backbone is in both arms and only Welireg is being decided. The org study id is Merck's own 6482 series, which is belzutifan, not the 3475 series, which is pembrolizumab

Velodrome, 'a 36-Week Refill Regimen': both arms are the Port Delivery System (Arm A Q36W against Arm B Q24W) and the interventions list the DEVICE 'Port Delivery System with Ranibizumab'. The study decides a refill interval for Susvimo; ranibizumab is the molecule inside the implant, not the product being tested

'Port Delivery System With Ranibizumab in Chinese Patients With Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration': the arms are Implant against IVT and the experimental intervention is the DEVICE 'PDS With Ranibizumab (100 mg/mL)'. Lucentis is the active comparator, and its 10 mg/mL intravitreal form is already labelled in nAMD

Sightspire, 'a 36-week Refill Exchange Regimen for the Port Delivery System With Ranibizumab': the single arm is the Port Delivery System, and the interventions list the DEVICE 'Susvimo PDS Implant'. Ranibizumab 0.5 mg intravitreal is only supplemental treatment. The study decides a refill interval for Susvimo, the same shape as Velodrome (NCT04657289), which is already pinned here.

AZURE-CHINA, 'A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Pharmacokinetics of AZD0780 in Participants With Dyslipidaemia': every EXPERIMENTAL arm is AZD0780, and rosuvastatin appears only as a run-in and background therapy, given in both the AZD0780 and placebo arms of Part A and Part B Cohort 2. The study landed on Crestor through the 'Rosuvastatin Dose 1' intervention name.
